declared.title: Mental contrasting for health behaviour change: a systematic review and meta-analysis of effects and moderator variables
declared.foundIn: scout notes on Manson's ideas (idea 3); Crossref search « mental contrasting health behaviour meta-analysis Cross Sheffield » (2026-11-23)

population: health-behaviour experiments (N = 1,528) of mental contrasting, alone or with if-then plans, against control

findings.text: Mental contrasting improved health behaviours up to four weeks later, with a small to moderate effect

support.sentence: A meta-analysis (N = 1528) using random effects modelling found a main effect of mental contrasting on health outcomes, adjusted Hedges' g = 0.28 (SE = .07), 95% CI [0.13-0.43], p < .001 at up to four weeks, and an increased effect at up to three months (k = 5), g = 0.38 (SE = 0.6), CI [0.20-0.55], p < .001.

findings.text: In a small subset of studies, adding if-then plans did not strengthen the effect of mental contrasting

support.sentence: Analysis on a small subset of studies suggested that the addition of implementation intentions (MCII) did not further strengthen the effects of mental contrasting on health behaviours, although additional studies are needed.

limits: few studies (5 at three months, 7 with if-then plans)
short follow-up: up to four weeks for the main effect
health behaviours only; countries not listed in the abstract
no sample from the Middle East or North Africa known
